title: Arroz con Leche
subtitle: Peruvian creamy rice pudding with cinnamon and cloves
excerpt: Peruvian arroz con leche is a rich, slow-cooked rice pudding made with whole milk, condensed milk and warm spices. The rice is simmered until thick and creamy, then dusted with ground cinnamon before serving. It is a comforting dessert eaten across Peru at all times of year.
sourceNotes: Arroz con leche arrived in Peru with Spanish colonists, who brought the rice pudding tradition from Moorish-influenced Iberian cooking. The Peruvian version is richer than the Spanish original, using condensed milk for extra sweetness and a combination of cinnamon and cloves for a warm, spiced flavour.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept in the fridge. Loosen with a splash of milk when reheating.

content.text: This recipe serves 6 and takes about 45 minutes from start to finish. Long-grain rice is simmered slowly in 1 litre of whole milk with a cinnamon stick and 3 cloves until very soft and thick. A tin of condensed milk is then stirred in along with lemon zest, giving the pudding its characteristic sweetness and richness.

Stir the pudding every few minutes as it cooks to prevent the rice from sticking to the bottom of the pan. Use a wide, heavy-based saucepan so the milk heats evenly. The pudding will continue to thicken as it cools, so pull it off the heat while it still looks slightly looser than you want the finished result to be.
Rinse 200g long-grain rice under cold water until the water runs clear. This removes surface starch and prevents the pudding becoming gluey.
Place the rice in a large, heavy-based saucepan with 1 litre of whole milk, the cinnamon stick and 3 cloves. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring to prevent the milk catching.

Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every 3 to 4 minutes, until the rice is very soft and the mixture has thickened to a porridge consistency. Keep the heat low enough to avoid the milk boiling over.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cloves. Stir in the condensed milk, 50g caster sugar and the zest of 1 lemon. Return to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Taste and adjust the sugar. Remove from the heat. The pudding should be thick but still pourable. It will set further as it cools.
Spoon into bowls or glasses. Dust generously with ground cinnamon. Serve warm or at room temperature.

attrs.symptom: Rice is sticking to the base of the pan
attrs.cause: Heat is too high or the pudding is not being stirred often enough
attrs.fix: Keep the heat at a low simmer and stir every 3 minutes. Switch to a heavier-based pan if scorching persists.

attrs.symptom: Pudding is too thick after cooling
attrs.cause: It was cooked too long before the condensed milk was added
attrs.fix: Stir in a splash of warm milk when reheating. Remove from the heat while the pudding still looks slightly thinner than the finished consistency you want.

attrs.cause: Condensed milk brands vary in sweetness
attrs.fix: Add the caster sugar gradually and taste as you go. Extra condensed milk also works, but will make the pudding richer.

content.text: Arroz con leche is eaten across all of Latin America, but the Peruvian version has its own character from the condensed milk and cloves. It is a dessert found in homes, school canteens and small restaurants, eaten any day of the week.
